name: Order Addition Permutation Optimization
summary: An outdated file check fails every submission, so later improvements are ignored
effect: Each submission's own score is unaffected. A run's reported best score is wrong whenever a later valid submission scores higher; how often this happened was not measured.

technical_finding: Integrity test expects a stale helper hash; every submission capped at pass rate 0.8, so pass_rate_first freezes the run on its first valid submission
technical_max_effect: material: later improvements ignored
validation_status: Paired runs (3, each exit=0): valid submissions pass 5/5 and the better later submission is selected, invalid controls rejected; a real archived run regraded through materialize.sh; package rebuilt from scratch on a clean machine (materialize-check-g2). name: PFR Formalization
summary: Five statements could never be earned because their type contained a hidden `sorry`
effect: Five targets cannot be earned (1.18 points); up to nine are affected when downstream proofs use them (2.13 points, inferred). The resulting 98.82 ceiling is an upper bound, not an attained score. Recovery on the actual targets and leaderboard impact have not been measured.
what_we_did: Candidate fix: the automatic arguments move into the five statements, which removes sorry from their types. Tests on similar lemmas pass; no proof of the five actual targets was run, and the solver image was not built.
technical_finding: Five scored statements carry a real sorryAx in their type (a `variable … := by volume_tac` measure binder in a Lean `module` file), so no proof can earn them, and every lemma whose proof uses them is also marked as depending on sorry; one theorem and its generated helper score identically in two tested styles (2/423); this does not establish fairness for all seven helpers
technical_max_effect: 1.18% unattainable (5/423, measured); up to 2.13% (9/423) for solvers following the upstream proofs (inferred from the measured rule and the upstream proof structure)
validation_status: Type-contamination mechanism validated on analogous lemmas; work image built once in the clean-machine rebuild (materialize-check-pfr, which ran a hand-edited copy of materialize.sh; the reordered committed materialize.sh has not been run), no solver run in it; actual five-target credit recovery unverified, because it needs real proofs of those theorems.

name: Portfolio Risk Calibration
summary: Excess return uses a slightly different formula than the instructions state
effect: Under its assumptions, a limited numerical search puts the change between −0.10 and +0.3921 points; this is not a bound for every case. In the side-by-side test the full score changes by +0.07 points. Lean shows that the fix keeps the sign and order of excess returns within the stated range.
what_we_did: The grader now subtracts the yearly returns, as the instructions say. A strategy tested side by side gains 0.07 points, and the wrong submissions tested still score zero. The numerical sweep and the Lean result on ordering both rest on stated assumptions about the range of inputs.
technical_finding: Annual excess computed as annualized difference of period returns, not the stated difference of annualized returns
technical_max_effect: Restricted numerical sensitivity envelope +0.3921 / −0.10 points; not a universal bound. Lean sign/order result has stated domain assumptions.
validation_status: Paired formula controls validated; 0.3921 is a restricted numerical sensitivity envelope, not a universal score bound.

name: Rust Multicrate Reconstruction
summary: Hidden tests that cannot compile zero two packages; fixed
effect: In the publisher's grading environment a complete, correct solution scores 73.99 out of 100, against 94.70 with the fix (+20.71); no submission can gain more than 29.2. Stopping at the first failing test file costs 0.4 to 3.3 points in the measured submissions. Graded with the published images as shipped, the same solution scores 27.6.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the hidden tests are placed where they compile, every test file runs, the earlier exemption fix is kept, and the missing vendored files are restored.
technical_finding: The grader inserts hidden tests where they do not compile, so cas-search (12 points) and cas-cli (10 points) score 0 for every solver who leaves the tests unchanged; Cargo stops at the first failing test binary and charges the unrun tests as failures; a passing exempt test can forgive one unrelated cas-pty failure. Public images only: the archive lacks 4 vendored cc files, so 9 of 14 crates cannot build (the publisher's own grading had them: restoring them reproduces its starter score 3.8189 exactly)
technical_max_effect: leaderboard (original grader + cc files, the publisher's environment, vs fixed): at most +29.22 for any submission (12 + 10 + 7.22 fail-fast exposure); measured +20.71 for a complete solution (73.9926 to 94.7022); fail-fast 0.43-3.26 measured; exemption fix at most -0.10. Public images: a complete solution scores 27.6091
validation_status: Three paired runs of the verbatim eval_cmd (each exit=0) reproduce every published score; TLA+ covers the exemption; v2 judge and work images rebuilt from scratch on a clean machine (materialize-check-rust). No solver build run in the v2 work image; the v2 starter arm ran once.

technical_finding: Phase 3 test checks callable() not identity
technical_max_effect: 1/160 of score (0.625 points), either direction
validation_status: Three paired runs (each exit=0): identity arm unchanged, wrapper arm -1/160, no-register arm as documented; package rebuilt from scratch on a clean machine (materialize-check-g2). name: Schemathesis Reporting Observability
summary: Two hidden tests give credit for wrong or broken output
effect: Wrong credit of about 2.4% of the total: 1/70 (about 1.4%) and 1/100 (1.0%); a correct writer with another suite name loses 1/70. The fixed version moves a score at most 4.76 points down, or 2.76 up (up to 4.76 only if a submission makes the GeneratedValue class unimportable).

technical_max_effect: ~2.4% wrong credit; fixed version moves a score by ≤4.76 down / ≤2.76 up (4.76 extreme)

One complete implementation tried; a namespaced JUnit root fails the revised test.

name: SMT Solver
summary: The answer checker misreads some valid solutions, so 27 hidden problems cannot be won
effect: A perfect solver's maximum falls from 78.61 to 72.40 (6.21 points). All solvers lose the 27 problems; those following the documented format also lose 42 more.
what_we_did: The fixed checker accepts the tested valid answers (with ground keys) on all 69 affected hidden files and rejects the tested wrong answers. The Lean soundness proof covers a restricted, modeled fragment of the checker, not every feature; compatibility with answers keyed by literal text has documented exceptions.
technical_finding: Witness checker keys UF values by source text, so 27 satisfiable hidden files are unwinnable; note (not part of the fix): the grader runs 16 solver processes at once under a 60 s wall-clock timeout (prompt says 16 evaluator workers, smtlib_spec.md:118 says 4); the official leaderboard configs set smt_solver judge_cpu_limit: 16, one CPU per process, but on a grader with fewer CPUs per-problem CPU shrinks proportionally (measured: at 4 CPUs a 20 CPU-s solver times out on every problem of a 32-problem subset)
technical_max_effect: perfect-solver max 78.61→72.40 (−6.21)
validation_status: Paired corpus controls validated; formal soundness covers only the modeled QF_UF fragment, with argued implementation correspondence.

name: Treant Forest
summary: The score scale tops out at 21 of 100 for any submission
effect: Every submission's score is squeezed into 0 to 21, with ordering kept. A simple, valid test submission scored 3.04.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: only the score scale changes, running straight from the starter's total (3,418) to the turn cap (92,304). Raw totals are identical; the same test submission now scores 16.36.
technical_finding: Anchors exceed the 2N² turn cap: max normalized 21.02; movement semantics question separate; note: at 4 grader CPUs (8 cases at once) a 55 s wall-deadline solver gets ~27 CPU-s per case vs ~55 at 8 CPUs; solutions using up to 58 s of CPU pass at 4 CPUs (slowest case 116.1 s < 120 s; measured); the README's full 60 s would sit at the 120 s limit
technical_max_effect: compresses all scores into 0–21; deadline solvers' scores depend on grader CPU count (unmeasured size)
validation_status: Anchor-only repair: raw scores identical under both versions in paired runs, greedy policy 3.04 -> 16.36 normalized, invalid control 0 in both; package rebuilt from scratch on a clean machine (materialize-check-g3). The 92,304 cap is a documented bound, not shown attainable.

name: Tree Block Partitioning
summary: The supplied grading library miscalculates when a value multiplies itself
effect: At most 5 of 100 points, only for submissions that multiply a value by itself. The other 95 points are unaffected.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: two lines in the grader's library swap order so both old values are read first. The reference solution still scores 100.
technical_finding: Supplied in-place multiply wrong when operands alias (v *= v)
technical_max_effect: ≤5/100 (T2), only for aliasing solvers
validation_status: Three paired runs (each exit=0): reference 100 -> 100, aliasing variant 0.25 -> 5, logic-error control unchanged; exhaustive aliased-state probe and TLA+ agree; package rebuilt from scratch on a clean machine (materialize-check-g2). How often real solvers write v*=v is unknown.

name: Triangulation Coloring Optimization
summary: The grader allows mesh moves the instructions forbid, and its test inputs overlap
effect: Changes which moves are allowed for every solver; how much a strong solver gains from forbidden moves was not measured. On a 4-CPU grader, solutions using about 15 to 30 seconds of CPU per case lost their whole score.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version (v2.2): forbidden flips are rejected, the test inputs are regenerated as complete triangulations (no overlaps, no gaps at the edge of the point set; the previous fixed version left gaps in 12 of 13 files), and the grader runs no more cases at once than it has CPUs. Scores are not comparable with the original.
technical_finding: Flip-legality rule omits the README's convexity condition; the same rule generated the cases (all 10 overlap/fold) and scores submissions; also the evaluator runs 8 cases at once under a 30 s wall-clock limit, so at the publisher's 4 grader CPUs a valid solution using 20 s CPU per case gets 8/10 TLE and TOTAL inf (measured; passes at 8 CPUs)
technical_max_effect: changes which flips are legal for every solver; size unmeasured (one flip: case 0009 644,809 → 641,611); up to the full score for solutions using ~15–30 s CPU per case on a 4-CPU grader
validation_status: Convexity, CPU and convex-hull coverage validated: all 13 v2.2 inputs cover their hull exactly (exact census); three identical paired runs of the original, v2.1 and v2.2 graders.

name: Trinity Text Adventure

name: Vibrating Path Graph Coloring
summary: On the publisher's 4-CPU grader, a solution within the 30-second limit can leave the whole submission without a score
effect: Up to the full score for solutions using about 14 to 30 seconds of CPU per case on a 4-CPU grader; solutions that stop at a deadline got half the computing time. The format mismatch has zero effect on 37 certified cases; its effect on the other 13 is unresolved.
what_we_did: The grader runs no more cases at once than there are CPUs, and grading gets 900 seconds. The format mismatch for zero-hit answers remains; its effect is ruled out on 37 certified cases and unresolved on the other 13. One failed case still voids the submission.
technical_finding: Evaluator runs 8 cases at once under a 30 s wall-clock limit; at the publisher's 4 grader CPUs (judge_cpu_limit: 4) a valid solution using 20–28 s CPU per case gets 2 OK + 48 TLE and TOTAL inf (no score) (measured; passes at 8 CPUs); the Python tester shares the CPUs (5.6–19.0 s per case) and once timed out a 25 s deadline solution's slow-tester cases (14 TLE; cause inferred, not observed; did not recur in the other eight original-grader gradings: jobs -b and -c, each run three times). Also: tester rejects documented 3-line zero-hit format (zero effect on 37 certified cases; 13 unresolved); one failed case voids submission (undisclosed)
technical_max_effect: up to full score for solutions using ~14–30 s CPU per case on a 4-CPU grader; deadline solvers get half the CPU; format mismatch has zero effect on 37 certified cases; 13 unresolved
validation_status: CPU controls validated; zero-hit formatting effect ruled out on 37 of 50 cases only, unresolved on the other 13.

name: Warehouse Forklift Routing
summary: Time limit is stricter than promised, and no score can exceed about 30
effect: A solver taking 60 to 150 seconds on any input, or more than about 30 seconds of CPU per input on the publisher's 4-CPU grader (half a CPU each under the 60-second limit), loses its whole score; every solver is capped at about 30.6 out of 100 (30.3 before display rounding).
what_we_did: The fixed grader raises each input's limit to 150 seconds and runs no more inputs at once than there are CPUs. It also needs the supplied change to how the harness waits, so that valid results arriving late are collected; this has not yet been tested end to end. The documented score ceiling stays.
technical_finding: Prompt promises 30 s per test case (150 s/input) but the evaluator gives 60 s per input; and a lower bound proved in Lean for a model of the tester (model matched to the tester by a 294-string differential test) shows every valid TOTAL ≥ 712.538 > rank1 395.80, so the top two anchors are unreachable and normalized scores are capped at ≈30.3; the evaluator also runs 8 inputs at once, so at the publisher's 4 grader CPUs a good-faith solver using 80–140 s CPU per input still got 2 OK + 48 TLE under the 150 s limit (measured)
technical_max_effect: whole score for budget-following solvers (60–150 s per input, or > ~30 s CPU per input at 4 CPUs, where each of 8 inputs gets half a CPU under the 60 s limit); ~70 points of the scale unreachable
validation_status: Grader time/CPU controls validated; requires harness wait overlay, whose end-to-end integration remains pending.
